usamts-2023-r1-01.prompt:
Fill each unshaded cell of the grid with a number that is either 1, 3, or 5. For each cell, exactly one of the touching cells must contain the same number. Here touching includes cells that only share a point, i.e. touch diagonally.

The grid is shown in the picture; below, shaded cells are drawn as $\blacksquare$:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0}\\\hline 1 & \phantom{0} & 1 & \phantom{0} & 3 & \phantom{0} & 5\\\hline \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \blacksquare & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0}\\\hline \blacksquare & \phantom{0} & 1 & 1 & 3 & 5 & \phantom{0}\\\hline \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \blacksquare & \phantom{0} & \blacksquare\\\hline \phantom{0} & \blacksquare & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0}\\\hline 5 & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & 5 & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0} & \phantom{0}\\\hline\end{array}$$

There is a unique solution, but you do not need to prove that your answer is the only one possible. You merely need to find an answer that satisfies the conditions of the problem.

usamts-2023-r1-02.prompt:
Suppose that the 101 positive integers
$$2024,\ 2025,\ 2026,\ \dots,\ 2124$$
are concatenated in some order to form a 404-digit number. Can this number be prime?
usamts-2023-r1-02.answer: **No.** Since $10^4 \equiv 1 \pmod{9999}$, the number is $\equiv 2024 + 2025 + \dots + 2124 = 101\cdot 2074 \pmod{9999}$, and $101 \mid 9999$, so the number is a multiple of $101$.

usamts-2023-r1-03.prompt: Let $n \ge 2$ be a positive integer, and suppose buildings of height $1, 2, \dots, n$ are built in a row on a street. Two distinct buildings are said to be *roof-friendly* if every building between the two is shorter than both buildings in the pair. For example, if the buildings are arranged $5, 3, 6, 2, 1, 4$, there are 8 roof-friendly pairs: $(5, 3)$, $(5, 6)$, $(3, 6)$, $(6, 2)$, $(6, 4)$, $(2, 1)$, $(2, 4)$, $(1, 4)$. Find, with proof, the minimum and maximum possible number of roof-friendly pairs of buildings, in terms of $n$.

usamts-2023-r1-04.prompt:
Prove that, for any real numbers $1 \le \sqrt{x} \le y \le x^2$, the following system of equations has a real solution $(a, b, c)$:
$$\begin{aligned} a + b + c &= \frac{x + x^2 + x^4 + y + y^2 + y^4}{2},\\ ab + ac + bc &= \frac{x^3 + x^5 + x^6 + y^3 + y^5 + y^6}{2},\\ abc &= \frac{x^7 + y^7}{2}. \end{aligned}$$
usamts-2023-r1-04.answer: Proof: $(a, b, c)$ are the roots of $P(z) = \frac{Q(z) + R(z)}{2}$ with $Q(z) = (z - x)(z - x^2)(z - x^4)$, $R(z) = (z - y)(z - y^2)(z - y^4)$. With $x \le y$, the sign changes of $P$ at $x, y, x^2, y^2, x^4, y^4$ give three real roots (degenerate cases $y = x$, $y = x^2$ directly).

usamts-2023-r1-05.prompt:
Let $A_1A_2A_3\cdots A_{13}$ be a regular 13-gon, and let lines $A_6A_7$ and $A_8A_9$ intersect at $B$. Show that the shaded area shown is half the area of the entire polygon (including triangle $A_7A_8B$).

In the picture, the vertices are labelled counterclockwise with $A_1$ at the top, so the chords $A_2A_{13}, A_3A_{12}, A_4A_{11}, A_5A_{10}, A_6A_9, A_7A_8$ are horizontal. The shaded regions are the trapezoids $A_2A_3A_{12}A_{13}$, $A_4A_5A_{10}A_{11}$ and $A_6A_7A_8A_9$; triangle $A_7A_8B$ hangs below the 13-gon.
usamts-2023-r1-05.answer: Proof: cancel three pairs of congruent triangles, reduce every remaining triangle to one with base $A_7A_8$ (height measured along the symmetry axis), and use two rhombi on the axis to show the heights balance: $2MD + MA_1 = 2MF + MC$.
